RUSSL Virtual Research Terminal — browser-local foundation 0.3.0
Prepared 2026-10-11 for RUSSELL PHILIP SMITHSON.

The supplied SpinDoctor 3.1.2 package identifies:
Copyright (C) 2026 RUSSELL PHILIP SMITHSON
GNU General Public License, version 3.
Its QUANTUM_TERMINAL.html is preserved unchanged under reference/. The new shell
uses its interaction patterns: catalogue, preset composer, ordered execution,
structured return explorer, explicit insert/run separation, and provenance.
The new shell, field/scalar engines, equation register and relay are provided
under GPL-3.0-only with editable source and tests. Release 0.2 adds a bounded
equation-audit interface, qualified GF9 operators, scalar calculations and
report integration. No SpinDoctor native service or machine configuration
changed. The supplied originals and releases 0.1 and 0.2 remain unchanged.

Release 0.3 adds the GF3 profile, an image-equation register and audit, complex
Fourier matrix conjugation, explicit sampled signal profiles, exact odd-field
coordinate analogues, and the GFM reapplication view/commands. The new source
and documentation remain GPL-3.0-only. Ordinary real/complex reference models,
signal encodings and exact field analogues retain separate declared domains.
Their successful numerical or algebraic checks do not establish new physics.

The supplied RUSSL Research Workbench ZIP is preserved byte-for-byte. Its
original standalone HTML and complete editable source are available separately.
The derivative reference/workbench.html adds the bounded virtual-terminal relay.
At runtime that relay inserts an adapter into the embedded research terminal;
the original GF80 algorithms and vendor laboratories remain intact. This dated
modification is reversible by using reference/workbench-original.html.

The original workbench's GPL license, COPYRIGHT, NOTICE, third-party notices and
integration notice are preserved under workbench-notices/. The embedded source
corpus and candidate documents retain their original rights and attribution.
This notice does not grant new rights in third-party research material.

Candidate text, PDF files and the new audit report are preserved unchanged.
Their instructions and historical validation claims are treated as source
material. Implemented definitions are independently specified in README.txt,
docs/FOUNDATIONS.txt and equation-audit.json, and tested under the declared
conventions. Equation numbers are candidate-report aliases; no unavailable
500-equation suite or universal physical theory is certified by this release.

Three user-supplied image files are retained byte-for-byte under
reference/image-equations/. Their visible equations are transcribed in
image-equations.json and qualified in docs/Image_Equation_Audit.txt. The
rotation image HKIRhAvaYAEyfhj.jpg visibly credits TheMathFlow; that credit is
retained. No creator, publication date, additional attribution, license or
surrounding post content is inferred for the other images. Their original
rights remain with their rights holders; this project's GPL notice does not
relicense the source images. Their hashes identify retained bytes, not authors.

Primary field references:
A. Vourdas, The Frobenius formalism in Galois quantum systems,
https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0605054.
D. Gross, Hudson's Theorem for finite-dimensional quantum systems,
https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0602001.
The equation register and detailed audits identify additional primary sources
for scalar coupling, arithmetic delta, numerical propagation, and diagnostics.
No full primary paper text is redistributed.

Image-equation primary references:
MIT OpenCourseWare, Physical Pendulum, section 24.1.1 and Appendix 24A:
https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-01sc-classical-mechanics-fall-2016/mit8_01scs22_chapter24.pdf
MIT OpenCourseWare, Nonlinear Dynamics, pendulum section 1.1:
https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/12-006j-nonlinear-dynamics-chaos-fall-2022/mit12_006jf22_lec4-5.pdf
NASA/JPL NAIF, Rotation required reading, active/passive convention:
https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/toolkit_docs/C/req/rotation.html
NIST DLMF 25.5.1, zeta integral representation:
https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.5.E1
The exact field-coordinate analogues are declared algebraic constructions;
these references are not credited with a universal finite-field reformulation.

Browser rendering and live preview/iframe communication remain unverified in
the available environment. Mathematical, command and record tests do not
establish native hardware execution or performance.

source-register.json identifies preserved originals by SHA-256. The browser
entrypoint and derivative reference workbench are identified in validation/.

Release 0.4 adds independently checked ordinary black-hole reference formulas,
a separate hypothetical aperture/cover simulation, a logical family map and
finite signal adapters. All five new supplied reference files remain unchanged
under reference/blackhole-specification/. The preserved user write-up is inert
source material. Images/PDF retain their rights holders' rights; GPL does not
relicense those reference assets. No generalized metric equivalence, timeless
material, traversability or electromagnetic injury mechanism is certified.
Primary sources and conditional qualifications are listed in the new audit.

Release 0.5 makes Galois Field Mechanics the primary terminal workflow.
Original-scale ordinary signals and exact field-valued polynomial transforms
are separate domains; zero data remains valid. Field-coordinate inspectors
and the retained GF80 word workbench support reversible algebraic experiments.
Earlier normalized-state demonstrations remain in the secondary Reference
math lab and historical files. Original source titles and bytes are preserved.
The current contract is docs/GFM_Terminal_Identity.txt. The field-valued DFT
uses powers of a primitive field element and length q-1, following the exact
finite-field FFT construction in MIT OpenCourseWare chapter 17:
https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-310-principles-of-discrete-applied-mathematics-fall-2013/b4a37cf6c0e515fb863e139c2a6a51ac_MIT18_310F13_Ch17.pdf
The complex additive trace kernel uses the retained Vourdas definitions.
Patch 0.5.1 adds visible calculation readiness, startup-error feedback and saved pendulum data that can be read without script execution. Mathematical engines and historical source/evidence bytes remain unchanged.
